THE ANALYTICAL FRAMEWORK

Four models. Explicit assumptions.

The workbench fits initial-rate measurements jointly across substrate and inhibitor concentrations using positive kinetic parameters.

Competitivev = Vmax·S / [Km·(1 + I/Ki) + S]
Uncompetitivev = Vmax·S / [Km + S·(1 + I/Ki)]
Noncompetitivev = Vmax·S / [(Km + S)·(1 + I/Ki)]
Mixedv = Vmax·S / [Km·(1 + I/Kis) + S·(1 + I/Kii)]

Interpret the comparison

AICc balances fit against model complexity. Lower values indicate stronger relative support; small differences leave multiple explanations plausible. Model weights describe support among these candidates, not probabilities of molecular truth.

Check the assumptions

These are classical steady-state inhibition models with an additive, constant-variance error assumption. They do not cover every inhibition process. Time dependence, assay interference, or systematic residual patterns may require another experiment or model.

Read the uncertainty

Parameter intervals are local, approximate estimates. Weakly identified parameters and boundary fits need particular care. A mechanism consistent with the observations is not proof of a binding site.

Design the next test

The design tool compares predictions of leading candidate models on a concentration grid. It prioritises disagreement within your chosen bounds and flags extrapolation beyond the observed range.
